redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py --selftest --stage at7-block` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 with 1 of 227 collected tests failing an assertion, the task's own among them (named by --case, HEAD's own tests green on HEAD's code), each passing with the working tree's implementation - pab1 (house FAIL): SELFTEST FAILED: 225/227 cases passed; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; the user's .npmrc in the home directory dropped (every run has a fresh home)

outcome.technical: add-phase, add-phase --from-file batch, and retarget now take --parent-branch <name>, validated in _parent_branch_refusal as an existing local branch before any write; add-phase writes phase.parentBranch and journals it under phase.add's details.parent, the batch path validates the key on phase.parentBranch the same way, and retarget writes it through _locked_retarget while refusing the flag once the phase already carries a branch (same reason --rename is refused there). _phase_entry's start-time fork refusal now names audit-task.py retarget <id> --parent-branch <branch> instead of the old dead-end sentence. Restored commands/phase.md step 4's removed sentence (Nothing measures whether you held the order when a gate is run by hand, needed by test__refs.py so3) and trimmed unrelated prose elsewhere in the file to stay at 3989/4000 bytes under tools/measure-context.py --gate's run-form ceiling, taking care not to touch substrings pinned by tools/prove-gates.py's phase_id_doc_drift row, test__proposals.py's ap5/ap6, or test__refs.py's rt1/so1-so4 (all re-verified green after each trim). plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py gained pab1-pab7 in _record_cases (stage at7-block): add-phase --parent-branch writes the phase with no branch cut yet and a ready task lands in it (pab1-pab2); start run from that branch forks the phase branch from it, recording baseRef, with parentBranch unchanged (pab3); a --parent-branch naming no local branch is refused with nothing written (pab4); retarget --parent-branch on a phase already on a branch is refused like --rename, field untouched (pab5); retarget writes parentBranch onto a branchless phase, journaled as a phase.retarget field move (pab6, the allow case); start's refusal on the wrong branch names --parent-branch by name (pab7). README.md's /audit:phase row and reference/manifest-conventions.md's phase-field list document the new flag and field. Ran python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py --selftest --stage at7-block: 231/231 cases passed. Ran python3 plugins/audit/tests/test__refs.py --selftest: 336/336 (so3 restored). Ran python3 plugins/audit/tests/test__proposals.py --selftest: 62/62 (ap5/ap6 fixed after reverting an over-aggressive trim of the Omit id sentence). Ran python3 tools/prove-gates.py --selftest: 37/37 (phase_id_doc_drift anchor intact). Ran python3 tools/measure-context.py --gate: GATE OK, run form 3989/4000. Ran python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --jobs 6 twice: first run (before the phase.md fix) showed 332/334 files ok with FAIL on test__proposals.py and tools/prove-gates.py, both caused by my own over-trimming of a pinned sentence; second run after the fix: 334/334 files ok, 16087 cases, exit 0.
outcome.descriptive: add-phase, its batch form, and retarget can now set a phase's parentBranch through a validated flag instead of a hand edit the plan gate used to refuse, and start's old dead-end refusal now names the verb that fixes it.
